dispatch: loaded before any Dispatch write (a message on the issue, the retro message).

findings.finding: Which issue the marker names is an inference that decides the file path: the parent spec says 'names this issue' (LEGSMOKE-1076 in its own words) and the child spec is empty.
findings.answer: Plan §1 and §8.1: the marker names LEGSMOKE-1079, following the convention on main where every earlier Stage 4b issue carries its own marker (smoke/LEGSMOKE-1069.md, smoke/LEGSMOKE-1070.md) and none names a parent key; recorded as the architect's decision, sent with the completion, proceeding is the default.

findings.finding: The acceptance criteria have no approved source (parent spec + empty child spec), and the spec may have been written since the facts were gathered.
findings.answer: Re-read dispatch doc-read --issue LEGSMOKE-1079 at plan-writing time (18:36Z): still empty, 90 bytes. Plan §1 names each criterion's source (parent spec quote, driver's message, title convention); §8.1 asks the architect to confirm the reading or write a child spec.

findings.finding: Retro's mandatory docs/solutions note lands on main and breaks the parent's 'no other path differs' literally; the slug is unknown at plan time.
findings.answer: Recorded as departure D1 (plan §7, specDepartures). AC3 has two checks: filtered compare from B equals the marker alone up to the approval; at retro's head and the merge commit the unfiltered compare lists exactly smoke/LEGSMOKE-1079.md and one docs/solutions/legion/*-LEGSMOKE-1079.md, no .legion/ path.

findings.finding: The recorded sha256 and byte count are a single point of failure; the plan must say which artefact is authoritative.
findings.answer: Plan §3: LINE is authoritative; every phase re-derives sha256/wc -c locally with printf '%s\n' and requires equality with the table and with the bytes read from the contents API; a disagreement is reported to the architect and the file is never edited to match a constant.

findings.finding: AC2's line count is event-dependent (one line, or two when a review asked), so it is not machine-checkable as one criterion, and the second line's text has no owner.
findings.answer: Plan §5 AC2 in two branches with exact checks: (a) wc -l=1, wc -c=85, tail byte 0a, sha256 constant, head -1 = LINE; (b) implementer appends, records the second line, new sha256, wc -c, wc -l=2 in implement.json at the new code head and re-runs the proof there; the second line's words are the review thread's own request as the reviewer wrote it.

findings.finding: A review finding asking for anything but the one appended line collides with 'no deferrals' and with AC3.
findings.answer: Plan §5 AC2: such an ask is answered on its thread as outside scope and sent to the architect with envoy_publish as a scope decision; never fixed by adding a path; the Fast-follow line holds nothing that would add one.

findings.finding: The tester's 'write the red test' rule has no landing place; a test file would itself violate AC3.
findings.answer: Plan §6 Tester step 3: break attempts are read-only API reads (404 at ref=main, independent .content route, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED at the trailered handoff head, case-variant path 404); no red test is written because ci.yml's check is sleep 20 && exit 0 with no checkout and any test file adds a path; recorded with the reason in test.json observations.

findings.finding: F equals B, so the 404 controls at F and B collapse into one read and cannot furnish two independent controls.
findings.answer: Plan §5 assigns distinct controls per phase: implementer 404 at ref=6d843f28 (stated as B = F) plus the altered-string mismatch; tester 404 at ref=main, the .content base64 route, and mergeStateStatus BLOCKED at the zero-check-run handoff head. .fail-me is forbidden in words with the reason: no root .gitignore, a probe would be snapshotted and turn the required gate red for every tree.

findings.finding: The production check after the close is unplanned, and for this change main is production; a 'pending' would idle the check to the 14-day bound.
findings.answer: Plan §5 AC5: main is production for a repository file; the implementer reads the marker at ref=<merge sha> and ref=main through the contents API, compares bytes, writes the Production: line naming the merge as the waking event plus one footer comment, verdict pass; pending is named as wrong here.

findings.finding: The PR body's CI line template names workflows this repository does not have (Tests, PR Title); only ci/check and fail-on-demand/gate exist and only gate is required.
findings.answer: Plan §5 AC4 and §6 Implementer step 5 give the CI line's exact shape naming the pull_request runs of fail-on-demand (gate) and ci (check) with the push pair beside them, verified by the check-runs read; Thermo omitted; Size: read from the filtered compare F...firstCodeHead; §6 retro bullet records that .github/ holds only workflows/.

findings.finding: The reviewer's required-set read may hit a branch-protection endpoint the App is refused (403 observed on branches/main/protection/required_status_checks).
findings.answer: Measured at 18:36Z: merge-gate.md's own protection read, repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/branches/main --jq '.protection.required_status_checks.checks[].context', succeeds and returns none (enabled false, checks []); the 403 is on branches/main/protection and .../protection/required_status_checks, which merge-gate.md does not use. Recorded in plan §4 fact 4 with the two reads separately.

findings.finding: Push sequence and the skip-checks: true trailer are per-phase and decide where CI exists; firstCodeHead is undefined.
findings.answer: Plan §6 and §9 fix the sequence: planner, implementer-handoff, tester and reviewer pushes are handoff-only and trailered; the implementer pushes the code first untrailered and records that SHA as firstCodeHead, opens the PR after it, and takes the proof after check-runs complete there; retro's push is untrailered. AC4 checks gate completed/success at firstCodeHead.

findings.finding: The branch guard cannot distinguish a proof-driver fixture commit from Legion's own, and B may stop being the branch tip.
findings.answer: Plan §3 records B and F (equal, with the SHA); §4's branch invariant adds an authorship read (jj log -r '<B>..@-' -T author.email()) and states the response: a commit no Legion App authored is a new pre-Legion tip B', judged from there, recorded as a departure, run proceeds; diverged/behind is a reset: stop and report. The stop condition is the four invalidating facts, never main's tip SHA; strict policy false, so no base update.

findings.finding: Every gh command in the plan is copied by the phases, so it must obey the pane wrapper's jq rule (no flag between --jq and the filter).
findings.answer: Plan §2 states the rule once as standing for every phase; every gh command in the plan puts jq flags inside the filter (| tostring, | @tsv). The plan reviewer checked each command.

findings.finding: AGENTS.md requires a fixture command before anything else in this repository, which the issue omits; several pre-state facts are live state each phase must re-read.
findings.answer: Plan §2 makes mkdir -p /tmp/legion-fixture && touch /tmp/legion-fixture/agents-md every phase's first step; §4 lists the four invalidating facts as commands each phase re-runs, with the planner's measured answers and times beside them; §3 marks the sha256/byte constants as derived from LINE.
